page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The full form
steps.margin_note: The expansion plus one line on what it does.
lines: PCR stands for POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION.
It makes many copies of a chosen DNA fragment,
in vitro, using primers and Taq polymerase.
steps.why: Chain reaction is literal: each cycle doubles the DNA made in the cycle before it, which is how thirty cycles reach a billion copies.
common_mistakes: Expanding it as 'protein chain reaction'. It is POLYMERASE chain reaction.
Saying it happens in a cell. PCR is done IN VITRO, in a tube.
steps.memory_tip: Each cycle doubles the DNA made in the cycle before it.

steps.label: Its uses
steps.margin_note: All three named uses, then the diagnostic one. Seven lines.
lines: It is also used to detect a disease before its
steps.why: All four uses need many copies of one small piece of DNA, which is exactly what PCR supplies.
common_mistakes: Giving only one use. Name all three — DNA cloning, gene amplification and DNA fingerprinting.
Confusing PCR with ELISA. PCR amplifies DNA; ELISA detects antigen-antibody binding.
steps.memory_tip: Anything that needs more DNA than you have.
